question: What safety and accessibility priority does the MUTCD establish for temporary traffic control planning and operation?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD establishes that road user and worker safety and accessibility should be an integral and high-priority element of every project involving temporary traffic control (TTC), from planning through design and construction. This priority extends to all road users — motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians (including those with disabilities), and workers — and is reflected in the seven fundamental principles of TTC, which call for safety comparable to normal highway conditions and minimal disruption to road user movement. Note that these provisions are Guidance (recommended practice), not mandatory Standards. Guidance (recommended): - Road user and worker safety and accessibility in TTC zones should be an integral and high-priority element of every project from planning through design and construction; maintenance and utility work should be planned and conducted with the safety and accessibility of all motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians (including those with disabilities), and workers considered at all times; if the TTC zone includes a grade crossing, early coordination with the railroad company or light rail transit agency should take place. - General plans or guidelines should be developed to provide safety for motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians, workers, enforcement/emergency officials, and equipment; the basic safety principles governing the design of permanent roadways and roadsides should also govern the design of TTC zones, with the goal of routing road users through such zones using geometrics, roadside features, and TTC devices as nearly as possible comparable to normal highway situations. - A TTC plan, in detail appropriate to the complexity of the work project or incident, should be prepared and understood by all responsible parties before the site is occupied, and any changes should be approved by an official knowledgeable in proper TTC practices; road user movement should be inhibited as little as practical, avoiding frequent and abrupt changes in geometrics that require rapid maneuvers. - Temporary traffic control operations should minimize the inconvenience, delay, and crash potential to affected traffic, and prior notice should be given to affected public or private agencies, emergency services, businesses, railroad companies or transit agencies, and road users before free movement is infringed upon or blocked. Citations: - Section 6A.02 Guidance §1 (p.766) - Section 6A.02 Guidance §2 (p.768) - Section 8A.13 Guidance §7 (p.992) - Section 6A.01 Support §3 (p.765) - Section 8A.13 Support §1 (p.992) - Section 1A.01 Support §1 (p.1)
gold_answer: Road-user and worker safety and accessibility must be treated as integral, high-priority considerations from planning through design and construction, including motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians with disabilities, workers, and coordination with rail transit where applicable.
